thread:
liam: Hey team — Acme reported that their org (tenant-acme-42) showed 0 credits ~3h before the monthly refill. They started getting 429s on generation endpoints. Scheduled refill according to billing is 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z but customer in America/Los_Angeles saw zero at 2026-02-28T16:05:00-08:00. Requesting quick triage steps and any known DST/timezone edgecases.
anna: Thanks. Can you paste the tenant id, plan, and a sample 429 response (curl) so we can see headers? Also did they purchase a top-up or change plan recently?
liam: tenant-acme-42, Pro-monthly. No recent plan change or top-up. Sample response:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-Id: req_01Fxxx
x-credits-remaining: 0
x-credits-reset: 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z
{
  "error": "quota_exhausted",
  "message": "Monthly credits exhausted"
}
```

Also sharing billing log snippet (redacted):
```
2026-03-01T00:00:00Z billing:tenant-acme-42 refill scheduled delta=100000
2026-03-01T00:00:01Z billing:tenant-acme-42 ledger updated balance=100000
```

liam: Customer says UI and API both showed 0 for a few hours before that scheduled time. They were on a long streaming session earlier in the afternoon (lots of reconnects).
anita: Two quick suspects: (1) UI/api cache in front of billing got stale and didn't pick up the ledger update, (2) streaming long-lived sessions + reconnects double-drew from the visible bucket in edge cache, then reconciler later fixed the ledger. Both are plausible. Can you run a couple of checks for me?
anita: 1) Redis key TTL + value for credits
2) ledger event search for tenant-acme-42
3) whether there were multiple concurrent sessions from same API key (reconnect storm)
anita: Commands you can run:
```
# check redis
redis-cli GET tenants:credits:tenant-acme-42
redis-cli TTL tenants:credits:tenant-acme-42

# fetch ledger events (internal)
jq '.events[] | select(.tenant=="tenant-acme-42")' /var/log/billing/ledger.log | tail -n 20

# quick api check
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer API_KEY" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/tenant-acme-42/credits" | jq .
```
liam: Ran them — redis key exists but value was 0 and TTL 3600. Ledger shows the refill lines (same as I posted). API /credits returned {"remaining":0}. So ledger shows refill at 00:00Z but visible stores still 0.
quota-bot: :rotating_light: billing-reconciler-failure tenant-acme-42 delta_mismatch=-1200 reconciler_id=rec-20260301-7 :rotating_light:
anita: That reconciler alert is helpful — indicates reconciler detected a negative delta and logged a failure. Root cause might be an interleaving race: streaming edge deducted from cache, reconciler tried to apply ledger delta but cache invalidation didn't propagate to the API layer, so API kept serving stale 0 until a manual sync.
anna: Sounds like a cache invalidation/sticky cache issue. Any quick mitigation so customer isn't blocked?
anita: Quick mitigation: force billing sync + clear cache for tenant. We have an admin endpoint to reconcile and flush tenant caches.

```
# admin sync (internal only)
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer ADMIN_KEY" \
  "https://admin.redwood.ai/internal/billing/sync?tenant=tenant-acme-42"

# flush tenant cache
POST https://admin.redwood.ai/internal/cache/flush
body: { "keys": ["tenants:credits:tenant-acme-42", "tenant:quota:tenant-acme-42"] }
```
anita: I'll run the sync now and watch logs. I'll also escalate to billing infra to investigate reconciler failure RH-4532.
anita: Running admin sync...

```
admin> reconciler rec-20260301-7 reconcile tenant-acme-42
admin> reconciler: applied delta +100001, new_balance=100001
admin> cache: flushed tenants:credits:tenant-acme-42
```
anita: After sync, API /credits returns {"remaining":100001}. Redis GET shows 100001, TTL refreshed.
liam: I pushed that to the customer — they confirmed their console now shows credits and can create new streams. They reported resumed generation without 429s. :white_check_mark:
anna: Great. Can you add the following to the support ticket: repro steps, redis/ledger outputs, reconciler alert id, and the admin sync command you ran? We'll need that for billing-infra.
liam: Added to ticket RH-4532 and linked the reconciler logs. Noted customer impact window ~2026-02-28T13:40-2026-02-28T16:07 PST. Marking customer notified.
anita: Follow-ups for infra team:
- Investigate why reconciler reported delta mismatch (-1200) and failed to atomically update both ledger and visible caches.
- Ensure cache invalidation propagated to API layer (edge caches + redis) on reconcile success.
- Check streaming reconnect path to ensure we don't double-debit transient sessions.
anna: Thanks everyone. I'll leave this thread open until billing-infra confirms a root cause. Assigned to @billing-infra, ticket RH-4532.

liam: Customer closed the incident on their side and wants to be kept posted on root cause. Closing the loop now but will reopen if it recurs.

anita: Noted. Filing a small postmortem item and adding an alert that flags reconciler delta mismatches > 1000 tokens so ops aren't reactive next time.

liam: Thanks :raised_hands:
